name: Valvular Heart Failure - Claims Optimized
remarks: Claims-optimized valvular heart failure module.
Designed for stronger BFD/CCW claim generation.
All major cost-generating actions occur within encounters.
Imaging studies converted to CPT procedures for better claims generation.
Includes ambulatory, emergency, inpatient, ICU, procedural utilization, and mortality.
Task 2.4 remediation (2026-08-10): valve surgery (Valve_Replacement,
an aortic valve replacement) previously happened with no valve
disease ever recorded -- HeartFailure_Onset only wrote generic
'Congestive heart failure'. Added Valve_Lesion_Type, a new branch at
the diagnosing encounter that records either aortic stenosis
(SNOMED 60573004) or mitral regurgitation (SNOMED 48724000);
Valve_Surgery_Check now gates the surgical arm on the aortic-
stenosis diagnosis (the only lesion this module's single surgical
procedure actually matches) so mitral-regurgitation patients take
medical management instead of an aortic valve replacement they
were never diagnosed to need.
Initial_Cardiology_Encounter chained four Medication_*_Supply_Delay
(30d each) + MedicationEnd states before closing -- the banned
Supply_Delay-while-open idiom (4 lint CRITICALs + open-across).
Furosemide, lisinopril, metoprolol, and spironolactone are chronic
GDMT drugs: ordered back-to-back same visit, chronic:true (engine
auto-renews annually), encounter closes right after the last
order -- same pattern as right_sided_heart_failure.json (Task 2.3)
and heart/chf_meds.json (Task 1.7).
Inpatient_Diuresis/Repeat_Diuresis had the same Supply_Delay idiom
on IV furosemide; recoded as administration:true injectable orders.
All CPT Procedure codes recoded to SNOMED-CT with hcpcs_code_map
rows preserving the original CPT billing; Critical_Care_Billing
(CPT 99291) deleted as redundant E&M billing, not recoded. Five
Observation states (Heart_Murmur + four *_BNP) carried raw
"value": {...} blocks that Gson silently drops -- every prior
BNP/murmur record was NULL. Fixed via top-level range (BNP) and
value_code (murmur). Added explicit EncounterEnds before both
Death branches (ICU and ward mortality checks), which previously
reached Death with the encounter still open.
Task 5.4 remediation (2026-08-10/11): this module's 'furosemide_rx'
and 'lisinopril_rx' attribute names didn't collide with any other
module's strings, but were generic enough to risk a future collision
(chf_meds.json/right_sided_heart_failure.json use differently-named
but semantically identical furosemide/lisinopril order attributes).
Prefixed 'vhf_' for consistency with those modules' Task 5.4 fixes --
verified by grep that no other module reads the new names.
Task 2.4: dropped the raw ICD-10-CM code entry -- GMF codes must be
SNOMED-CT (ICD-10-CM is not in the scanner's OK_SYSTEMS set and was
a bad-system finding); export layer already derives the ICD-10 from
the SNOMED code via condition_code_map.json.
Task 2.4: new branch. Aortic stenosis and mitral regurgitation are
the two most prevalent valve lesions progressing to heart failure
in this age group (Nkomo VT et al., 'Burden of valvular heart
diseases: a population-based study', Lancet 2006;368:1005-11) --
modeled here as a roughly even split between the two, slightly
favoring aortic stenosis since it's the more common indication for
surgical intervention in the elderly and this module's only
surgical procedure (Valve_Replacement) is an aortic valve
replacement. Split itself is a first-pass estimate, not a precise
replication of the cited study's age-stratified prevalence.
Task 2.4: this module's only surgical procedure (Valve_Replacement)
is coded as an aortic valve replacement, so mitral-regurgitation
patients are gated out of Valve_Surgery_Check's surgical arm (see
its remark) and always take the medical-management path -- avoids
billing an aortic valve replacement on a patient whose diagnosed
lesion is mitral, which the pre-fix module had no way to prevent
(it never recorded a lesion at all).
Task 2.4: a raw `"value": {...}` block is not a recognized GMF
field -- Gson silently drops it and every prior record here was
NULL. Qualitative exam finding, so the fix is `value_code`, not a
numeric range (same fix as right_sided_heart_failure.json's
JVD_Observation, Task 2.3).
Task 2.4: recoded from CPT 93306 (bad-system) to the standard
transthoracic-echo SNOMED concept (same recode as
right_sided_heart_failure.json, Task 2.3 -- see its remark on the
hcpcs_code_map.json 93306 addition).
Task 2.4: recoded from CPT 71046 to SNOMED 399208008, which already carries the correct 71046 hcpcs_code_map row.
Task 2.4: hoisted the raw `value` block into a top-level `range`.

Task 2.4: recoded from CPT 71045 to a distinct SNOMED concept from

remarks: Task 2.4: IV diuresis during an admission is a hospital
administration event, not a filled outpatient prescription -- fixed
the same way as right_sided_heart_failure.json's Inpatient_Diuresis
(Task 2.3): recoded from oral 313988 to injectable RxCUI 1719286
with administration:true (no assign_to_attribute/MedicationEnd).
Task 2.4: gated on the Valve_Lesion_Type diagnosis (new, see that
state's remark) -- this module's only surgical procedure is coded
as an aortic valve replacement, so only patients diagnosed with
aortic stenosis are eligible for it. Mitral-regurgitation patients
always take medical management (matches real-world practice: MR is
managed medically far more often than AS, which is the classic
'surgery is not optional once severe/symptomatic' valve lesion).
Pre-fix, this ran unconditionally and could send ANY valvular-HF
patient to Valve_Replacement with no valve disease ever recorded.
Task 2.4: recoded from CPT 33405 (bad-system) to SNOMED; added the
hcpcs_code_map.json row (26212005 -> 33405).
Task 2.4: used to route through a separate Critical_Care_Billing
Procedure (CPT 99291, bad-system) first. Deleted rather than
recoded, same call as right_sided_heart_failure.json's ICU_Admission
(Task 2.3): a standalone 'critical care first hour' charge for time
already covered by this same ICU encounter is redundant billing.
Task 2.4: new state. ICU_Mortality_Check used to jump straight to
Heart_Failure_Death with ICU_Admission still open -- Death is a
valid closer per the lint tool's own model, but the graph walk
still flagged the death state as reachable in both open and closed
encounter contexts. Explicit close before Death, same pattern used
in right_sided_heart_failure.json (Task 2.3) and Task 1.1's CRPC
death path.
Task 2.4: same IV-administration fix as Inpatient_Diuresis -- see its remark.
Task 2.4: new state -- same both-context Death fix as ICU_Death_End
above, for the ward-level (non-ICU) mortality check.
Moderate-to-severe valvular heart disease affects roughly 2-3% of
adults (around 10% over 75). The age Guard alone admits every
patient over 50, which made "Congestive heart failure" onset in
84% of the cohort.
Task 2.4: rate sourcing note (this state's own probability is
unchanged -- out of this task's scope, which is encounter/coding
defects and the valve-diagnosis gap, not full epidemiological
recalibration). Cited to Nkomo VT et al., 'Burden of valvular heart
diseases: a population-based study', Lancet 2006;368:1005-11
(moderate-or-greater valve disease ~2.5% overall, rising sharply
with age). Rate is a first-pass estimate and needs clinical review;
no target share was specified for this module in the Phase-2 fix
spec.
CROSS-MODULE GATE (audit Class 7, task 5.2 group 4) -- the heart-failure
quartet. Four top-level modules each diagnose their own heart-failure code
with no coordination, so one patient could carry all four at once and run
four competing maintenance/decompensation loops against them:
congestive_heart_failure.json   88805009 Chronic congestive heart failure
high_output_heart_failure.json  10091002 High output heart failure
right_sided_heart_failure.json  10335000 Chronic right sided heart failure
valvular_heart_failure.json     42343007 Congestive heart failure
Rule: FIRST-TO-DIAGNOSE WINS. Each module tests the other three codes on its
own onset path; whichever module gets there first owns the patient's heart
failure and the other three stand down.
Only the primary code of each rival is tested. That is not a shortcut: the
record key is codes[0] (HealthRecord.conditionStart keys `present` by
primaryCode), so high_output_heart_failure.json's secondary ICD-10 entries
I50.9 / I50.89 never enter `present` and cannot be matched by an Active
Condition check. No module in the tree emits a ConditionEnd for any of these
four codes (verified by grep), so once one is set the other three modules'
checks stay true for life.
This is the EARLY gate. It sits before the cardiology encounter opens, so a
patient who already has a heart-failure diagnosis from a rival module never
gets this module's workup visit, its echo/BNP/imaging or its drug orders. No
encounter is open at this point, so Terminal leaks no encounter lock.
It is not sufficient on its own: State$Encounter.process returns false --
blocks across ticks -- while another module holds this person's encounter
lock, so the verdict here can go stale. The recheck below re-tests once the
encounter has actually opened.
CROSS-MODULE GATE (audit Class 7, task 5.2 group 4) -- the heart-failure
quartet. Four top-level modules each diagnose their own heart-failure code
with no coordination, so one patient could carry all four at once and run

high_output_heart_failure.json  10091002 High output heart failure
right_sided_heart_failure.json  10335000 Chronic right sided heart failure
valvular_heart_failure.json     42343007 Congestive heart failure

Only the primary code of each rival is tested. That is not a shortcut: the

This is the LATE gate, and it is the one that makes the exclusion airtight.
It is the only predecessor of the ConditionOnset, that ConditionOnset has no
target_encounter (so it records its code the moment it processes), there is
no Delay or blocking state in between, and module processing is
single-threaded per person per tick. No rival can diagnose between this test
and this module's own diagnosis, in either ordering.
A hit here leaves the patient one cardiovascular-examination encounter with
no clinical content; it is closed explicitly rather than abandoned.
Closes the Initial_Cardiology_Encounter encounter when the cross-module heart-failure
recheck hands the patient to whichever module diagnosed first.
Required, not cosmetic: going to Terminal with the encounter still
open would hold this person's encounter lock for the rest of their
life -- the Class 6 defect the audit recorded against this very
module family (high_output_heart_failure.json).
